findings.title: Busy times and bookings are ignored for slots inside a date override
findings.description: When a slot falls inside a date-override window, `dateOverrideExist` is set to true (line 113). The function then returns `true` at lines 133–135, before `busy.every(...)` at line 153 runs. Calendar events and existing bookings in `busy` are never checked for that slot. Both the fixed-host pass (`getSchedule`, lines 485–498) and the loose-host pass (lines 513–518) rely on this function for busy checks, so double-booking is possible on any day that has a date override. The override should only narrow the window, and the slot should then fall through to the busy check. The "Check for Date overrides" test (`apps/web/test/lib/getSchedule.test.ts:742-805`) has no busy times, so it does not catch this.

findings.title: Every slot on a weekday with split working hours is rejected
findings.description:
`workingHours.find(...)` returns truthy when any block on that weekday does not contain the slot start (lines 139–147). `getWorkingHours` (`packages/lib/availability.ts:76-124`) emits one entry per availability row, so a split shift such as Mon 09:00–12:00 plus 13:00–17:00 gives two Monday entries. Any slot is outside at least one of them, so every slot that day is rejected. `getSlots` already handles multiple blocks (`packages/lib/slots.ts:170-204`), so the new check is redundant for single-block days and destructive for split-shift days.

Line 142 also sets `end` from `slotStartTime` instead of `slotEndTime`. The end check therefore repeats the start check, and slot length is ignored.

The only multi-row fixture, `IstWorkHoursWithDateOverride` (`getSchedule.test.ts:107-129`), has its second block on the override date. The override branch returns before this check runs, so no test reaches the multi-block path.

findings.title: Multiple override ranges on one date reject every slot on that date
findings.description:
The same inverted `find` logic applies to date overrides. The predicate returns true, meaning "not available", whenever the slot is outside any same-day override (lines 117–125). `getUserAvailability` creates one date override per dated availability row with no grouping (`packages/core/getUserAvailability.ts:215-224`). Two disjoint ranges on one date, such as 09:00–12:00 and 14:00–17:00, therefore reject every slot that day.

The predicate also uses `find` for side effects: `dateOverrideExist` is set inside it (line 113). `some` with explicit accept logic would be clearer.

findings.title: Identity comparison makes the zero-length override branch unreachable
findings.description: `dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)` compares two object references, so it is always false and the branch at lines 114–116 never runs. If the intent is that a zero-length override excludes the slot, use `.isSame(...)`. Without it, a slot that overlaps a zero-length override is treated as available.

findings.title: Date-day match depends on the server's local timezone
findings.description: `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` is in process-local mode. `@calcom/dayjs` sets no default zone (`packages/dayjs/index.ts:14-23`), so `.format("YYYY MM DD")` reads the server's local calendar date. `slotStartTime` (line 100) is UTC. The day match is only correct when the server runs in UTC. `dayjs.utc(date.start).add(...)` keeps both sides in UTC.

findings.title: Per-slot `dayjs.tz` calls on the hot path
findings.description: The predicate calls `dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset()` for every override before it checks the day. `checkIfIsAvailable` runs for every slot and every fixed host (`getSchedule`, lines 485–498), and `dayjs.tz` goes through `Intl` formatting. Compute each override's shifted start and end once, or filter by day before computing the offset.

findings.title: Override times lose their day when shifted across midnight
findings.description: The override is selected for an invitee day using its unshifted start (line 207). The times are then shifted by the invitee–organizer offset and reduced to minutes-of-day (`hour()*60 + minute()`), which drops the date. Example: organizer `Asia/Kolkata` has an override 03:00–04:00 on Nov 23, and the invitee is UTC. The override is selected for Nov 23. The shifted start is 21:30 on Nov 22, but it is placed at 21:30 on Nov 23. An override that becomes end-before-start is silently dropped by the `start >= end` skip at line 68.

findings.title: Optional `timeZone` on the shared type is silently defaulted
findings.description: `TimeRange.timeZone` is optional (`packages/types/schedule.d.ts:5`). `override.timeZone` can therefore be undefined, and `.tz(undefined)` falls back to dayjs's default zone without an error. I did not verify that fallback in node_modules, which is absent. `getSchedule` always sets the value, but `getSlots` accepts overrides without it. Line 212 also round-trips a `Date` through `Date.toString()`, which drops milliseconds, while line 219 uses `dayjs(override.start)` directly. A dedicated override type with required `timeZone` would make the contract explicit.

findings.title: The new availability logic has no targeted tests
findings.description: The only added test (`apps/web/test/lib/getSchedule.test.ts:788-804`) changes the invitee timezone for one override day. Nothing covers a busy event on an override day, split working hours, multiple override ranges, a zero-length override, or an override that crosses midnight after the timezone shift. Each of the first three findings and the midnight case would be caught by a small test. The comment at line 798 ("it should return the same as this is the utc time") also does not say what property is being checked.

findings.title: Whitespace churn and an ineffective timezone argument in the selected-slots pass
findings.description: Two blank lines were removed, around lines 178 and 591, with no functional change. The selected-slots pass (lines 579–586) passes `organizerTimeZone` but not `dateOverrides` or `workingHours`, so the timezone has no effect there. Either pass the overrides for consistency or drop the lookup. The inline `dateOverrides` type at lines 87–90 also duplicates `TimeRange`.
